q: Define relative atomic mass.
a: The ratio of the average mass of one atom of an element to one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. It has no unit.

Define atomicity.
a: The number of atoms present in one molecule of an element or compound. Example: O₂ is diatomic, O₃ triatomic, P₄ tetratomic.

Give the salient features of modern atomic theory.
a: 1) An atom is no longer indivisible; it is made of protons, neutrons and electrons. 2) Atoms of the same element can have different masses (isotopes, e.g. ₁₇Cl³⁵ and ₁₇Cl³⁷). 3) Atoms of different elements can have the same mass (isobars, e.g. ₁₈Ar⁴⁰ and ₂₀Ca⁴⁰). 4) Atoms of one element can be changed into another by transmutation. 5) Atoms may not combine in simple whole-number ratios (e.g. sucrose C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁). 6) The mass of an atom can be converted into energy (E = mc²). 7) The atom is the smallest particle that takes part in a chemical reaction.

q: Derive the relationship between relative molecular mass and vapour density.
a: Vapour density = mass of a volume of gas ÷ mass of the same volume of hydrogen. By Avogadro's law equal volumes have equal numbers of molecules, so VD = mass of 1 molecule of gas ÷ mass of 1 molecule of H₂ = mass of 1 molecule ÷ (2 × mass of 1 H atom). Relative molecular mass = mass of 1 molecule ÷ mass of 1 H atom. Therefore 2 × vapour density = relative molecular mass.
